segment_text: 2.6Quality Agreement. As soon as reasonably practicable after the Effective Date, the Parties shall agree to the terms and conditions of a quality agreement (the “Quality Agreement”) setting forth in detail the quality assurance arrangements and procedures for the Manufacture of the Product, which Quality Agreement shall be incorporated herein by reference. For clarity, the Parties shall agree to the terms and conditions of (a) the Quality 5 ​ Agreement for the Product for Development use as soon as reasonably practicable after the Effective Date, and (b) the Quality Agreement for the Product for Commercial uses, if different than the Quality Agreement specified in subsection (a), as soon as reasonably practicable after the first MAA for the Product is submitted in the Kissei Territory; provided that the Quality Agreement may be amended if mutually agreed by the Parties. To the extent that the terms of this Supply Agreement and those of the Quality Agreement are in conflict, the terms of this Supply Agreement shall control except with respect to quality issues, which shall be governed by the Quality Agreement. For clarity, if there are any financial terms in the Quality Agreement that are in conflict with this Supply Agreement, this Supply Agreement shall control with respect to such financial terms.
conditions: if different than the Quality Agreement specified in subsection (a)

annotator_notes:
S3 limb (b) of E03-022 -- the SECOND of the segment's two items.

SEGMENT ELIGIBILITY, because this item cannot be read without it. E03-022 is 1,321 characters over 5 sentences with 7 modal tokens, and its clause count was the eligibility question. RULED: TWO obligation-bearing clauses, within section 2's 1-3 band. S1 is a heading fragment. S2's duty is NOT_ANNOTATABLE under section 4.3.1 STEP 2 (see below). S2's trailing 'which Quality Agreement shall be incorporated herein by reference' is a legal-effect clause with a non-party subject. S3's proviso is EXCLUDED as a savings/reservation provision (exclusions.json, E03-022#amendment-proviso) -- and that exclusion is what keeps the count at 2 rather than 3. S4 and S5 are conflict-precedence provisions with non-party and Agreement-as-subject, section 8.8's own named class, the same as C03-102 / C12-017 / C02-062.

THE DUTY IS ANNOTATABLE AT ALL ONLY BECAUSE OF A DISCRIMINATOR DRAWN FOR THE FIRST TIME AT THIS SEGMENT. REVIEWER-RULED 2026-09-25. 'the Parties shall agree to the terms and conditions of a quality agreement' is an AGREEMENT-TO-AGREE, and the two committed precedents point OPPOSITE WAYS: C05-043 and C04-101 were EXCLUDED as agreements-to-agree ('its content is not readable at segment scope until a separate agreement exists', ratified at B4 as citable to section 2's amended cross-reference test), while C04-02 is a LOCKED ITEM with action NEGOTIATE drawn from 'the Parties will negotiate in good faith which Party(ies) is/are responsible for payment' -- an agreement-to-agree with an equally undetermined outcome. NEITHER PRECEDENT HAD EVER BEEN DISTINGUISHED FROM THE OTHER.

  THE DISCRIMINATOR, and it is sharper than 'is the duty's content readable', since BOTH cases have indeterminate outcomes: IS THE DUTY ITSELF THE ACT OF REACHING AGREEMENT, or is some OTHER, SEPARATE duty conditioned on a future agreement existing?
    - The duty IS reaching agreement -> ANNOTATABLE. action, obligor and object_class are all fully readable from the span, even though the eventual agreement's CONTENT is not. C04-02's shape, and this item's.
    - A SEPARATE duty is qualified by a future agreement -> EXCLUDED. The qualifier sits on top of a DIFFERENT obligation and makes THAT obligation's own content unreadable. C05-043's shape ('to the extent permitted by applicable law and AS MUTUALLY AGREED BY THE PARTIES', where the primary duty was something else entirely).
  Here, as in C04-02, there is no separate duty being qualified: 'reach agreement on the Quality Agreement's terms' IS the entire obligation, and it is fully determinate as a DESCRIPTION OF REQUIRED CONDUCT. Recorded as forward guidance in this item and in section 10.1 F26 rather than as a section 2 amendment, the same disposition E03-046's C11-079/C03-01 discriminator took.

SECTION 4.3.1 STEP 2's FIRST MATERIAL INSTANCE, APPLIED AS DESIGNED -- NOT STRETCHED. Step 2 has carried 'STATUS: UNTESTED -- no instance has arisen in any material seen so far' since v0.28, with the warning that it 'must not borrow confidence from step 1'. This segment is its first real application and it fits the rule AS ALREADY WRITTEN. S2 states the duty GENERALLY ('a quality agreement'); S3, TAKEN AS A UNIT, restates it COMPLETELY -- limb (a) and limb (b) together specify exactly what S2 leaves general, naming both quality agreements and both deadlines. STEP 2's TEST IS COMPLETENESS, AND COMPLETENESS DOES NOT REQUIRE THE MORE-COMPLETE STATEMENT TO BE A SINGLE CLAUSE: it requires that the statement, taken as a unit, fully specifies the obligation the redundant span only gestures at. That is precisely what S3(a) + S3(b) do. So S2's duty span [22:291] is marked NOT_ANNOTATABLE (section 4.4) and recorded verbatim with offsets in the segment file, exactly as step 2 prescribes.

  THIS IS VALIDATION OF STEP 2's DESIGN, NOT A STRAIN ON IT, and the framing is the reviewer's ruling rather than a drafting choice. Reading it as 'step 2 extended to a 1:2 shape' would understate how directly it fits.

  WHY NOT THE ALTERNATIVES, both of which were drafted and put to the reviewer. THREE ITEMS (step 1's literal 'any scored field differs' test, which returns "distinct" because the object restrictions differ) DOUBLE-COUNTS THE REAL-WORLD ACT: agreeing the Development-use Quality Agreement would satisfy both S2's item and S3(a)'s, so a model sensibly emitting two candidates eats a MISSED -- precisely the failure section 4.3.1 exists to prevent. ONE ITEM ON S2, marking S3 NOT_ANNOTATABLE, was rejected because it DISCARDS S3(b)'s genuinely different trigger (the first MAA submission), real content S2 does not carry.

  S2's DUTY IS NOT A DISCARDED DRAFT. It was drafted and presented in full before the segment's structure was understood; NOT_ANNOTATABLE is its CORRECT disposition once the whole segment is read, not a reversal of an error.

ACTION: 'agree' IS A GENUINE SECTION 8.8 GAP. REVIEWER-RULED 2026-09-25, and the ground is the VERB'S OWN SEMANTICS rather than the absence of mapping evidence -- recorded that way deliberately, because the discriminator generalises to any future collective-duty verb.

  THE RULE THIS TURNS ON: 'agree' HAS BILATERAL MUTUAL ASSENT BUILT INTO ITS MEANING. A single party cannot 'agree' to terms -- it can PROPOSE them, or FINALIZE a draft -- so the plurality is carried by the verb itself, not by who happens to be performing it. FINALIZE does not denote that performance: one party can finalize a document alone. Under section 8.8.2's same-performance test the mapping therefore loses something real.

  AND IT IS A STRONGER FAILURE THAN SECTION 8.8.2's OWN WORKED CASE, which is why the distinction is worth naming rather than filing as 'another near-miss'. 'defend' failed against INDEMNIFY because a duty to defend carries PRACTICAL MACHINERY (conducting a defence) the member lacks -- a fact about what the duty involves. 'agree' fails against FINALIZE because the verb's own SEMANTICS REQUIRE PLURALITY -- a fact about what the word means. VERB SEMANTICS REQUIRING PLURALITY versus PRACTICAL MACHINERY REQUIRING PLURALITY are two different grounds for the same test coming out NO, and a future collective-duty verb should be checked against both.

  NEGOTIATE WAS RULED OUT FIRST, ON MEASURED CORPUS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN INTUITION -- section 8.8.2's discriminator 1, with the detector gated on section 8.8.2's OWN cited instance ('failed to defend or indemnify', which reproduces in exactly 1 segment) before any count was read off it. THE CORPUS ENUMERATES THE TWO AS SEPARATELY-FAILABLE DUTIES: C04-119's 'the Parties shall CONSULT each other, NEGOTIATE in good faith and AGREE in writing upon an adaptation' lists three, with 'agree' as the CULMINATING act after the other two; C04-101 pairs 'NEGOTIATED in good faith and mutually AGREED upon'. Same evidence shape as section 8.8.2's 'failed to defend or indemnify' and section 8.8.3's 'withheld, conditioned or delayed'. Mapping agree -> NEGOTIATE would also assert something WEAKER than the contract (the process instead of the outcome) -- the mirror of section 8.8.3's defer -> WITHHOLD rejection, which was refused for asserting something STRONGER.

  STATED AGAINST INTEREST, on section 8.8.3's own discipline: NO BASE RATE IS CLAIMED FOR THE MAPPING TARGET. 'finali*' occurs in only 3 of the 1,547 pool segments across 2 documents, and NONE enumerates 'finalize' and 'agree' as separately-failable duties -- so discriminator 1 returns NO EVIDENCE here rather than evidence of mappability, and the ruling rests on the semantic ground above, not on that silence. Same posture section 8.8.3 took for 'defer' (1 occurrence) and E02-02 for 'generate' (11 segments).

  CONSEQUENCE: action holds the NEAREST member, FINALIZE; action_accept_set is the SECTION 8.8 SINGLETON ['FINALIZE'], no widening; the real verb 'agree' is recorded verbatim here; known_gaps gains action_not_in_taxonomy. Section 8.8.5's G9 forced-choice disclosure applies to this item wherever criterion-2 figures are reported -- clause 2 here is an agreement check, not an action-identification measurement.

OBJECT_CLASS: 'commercial_quality_agreement'. Head noun 'Agreement', head-only member 'agreement' per section 3.6's v0.58 rule; parallel prefix per section 4.3.2's naming convention (see the sibling E03-04). SECTION 3.6.1 AND 3.6.2 BOTH CLEAR.

CONDITIONS -- ONE ENTRY: 'if different than the Quality Agreement specified in subsection (a)'. It passes section 3.8.2's removal test cleanly: delete it and the duty to agree a Commercial-use Quality Agreement applies UNCONDITIONALLY, which is a different duty, so it is a genuine gate rather than object scope. Its internal cross-reference ('subsection (a)') needs no resolution and does not exclude -- section 2's v0.28 carve-in covers a cross-reference inside verbatim-quoted condition text, and this one resolves INSIDE the span in any case, since limb (a) is part of it.

SHARED_SUBJECT_SPLIT (section 8.3.1, v0.31 option 4). S3's subject and modal sit in a stem both limbs share ('For clarity, the Parties shall agree to the terms and conditions of'), so this item's span runs CONTIGUOUSLY FROM THE SHARED SUBJECT THROUGH THE END OF ITS OWN LIMB and therefore properly CONTAINS the sibling's span -- option 4 exactly, adopted because option 3 (the limb alone) is mechanically unreachable, its obligor falling outside span_text and being rejected as NESTED_FIELD_NOT_IN_SPAN.

  THE FIRST shared_subject_split THAT COSTS NOTHING AT ALIGNMENT, and it is worth recording as such. Section 8.3.1 states option 4's cost plainly: C14-076's nested pair sits at IoU 0.689, ABOVE section 4.1's 0.5 threshold, so a model emitting only one span makes the pairing genuinely ambiguous and one item is MISSED. HERE THE NESTED IoU IS 192/436 = 0.440, BELOW the threshold -- computed, not estimated -- so these two spans CANNOT mis-align to each other and option 4's accepted limitation does not bite. C14-02 was the only locked carrier of this tag until now; this is the second, and the two are not comparable on that cost.

MUTUAL_OBLIGATION DOES NOT FIRE, worked through section 8.4.2's procedure IN ORDER rather than read off the 'the Parties' surface form, which that section's marker-regex paragraph warns against. (a) modality duty-bearing: MUST, PASSES. (b) binds two or more parties: 'the Parties' is the collective form the test names, PASSES. (c) the obligee is that same counterparty: NO obligee is stated, and 'obligee: ABSENT is a FAILURE, not a deferral'. FAILS. No tag. Identical outcome and identical failing test to C04-02, which is also a collective-subject agreement-to-agree.
